just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on D4 and dwells most on D in Nastari. The line peaks at G4 (384.6 Hz) at 1:18.9. It closes on Ek4, not the tonic (D3 → C4 → G4 → G4 → D4 → Ek4).

theory_fit.name: Vaziri 24-tone equal temperament
theory_fit.description: Quarter-tone grid (koron/sori = exactly 50 ¢ from the natural note).

theory_fit.name: Pythagorean / Safi al-Din
theory_fit.description: Nearest note of the 17-note gamut generated by pure fifths (±8) from the tonic.

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic G set in the catalog (the Nava suite's finalis G (as in Alizadeh's setar radif of the same dastgah, on E, moved to Shahnazi's pitch); the vote picked the 5th. Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 285.7 Hz (D)

p02 (A): E2 window sizes disagree by 14 ¢ {4096: 203.35, 8192: 189.07}; the shorter window reads higher: a string ringing near the note pulls the shorter window toward it, short notes blur the longer one
